cards.explanation: The answer is His own angel. Verse 1 says Jesus Christ sends His angel: “He made it known by sending His angel to His servant John…” So this message came by special delivery, friends. I once had an angel show up at the junk drawer I was stuck in, so I know how a visit like that goes.

The answer is False. John doesn't hand this over as his own opinion. He says he testifies to everything he saw, and then he calls it “…the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ.” This is a man reporting what he saw, friends, not telling you what he feels like thinking.

The answer is those who hear and obey it. The blessing goes to the reader and also to “…those who hear and obey what is written in it…” Hearing and obeying go together, friends. I'm happy to bake with anybody who signs up for both.

The answer is Jesus Christ. The grace and peace come from the One who is and was and is to come, from the seven spirits before His throne, and from Jesus Christ. Verse 5 then calls Him “…the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth.” That's a whole list of titles for one name, friends.

The answer is dead. Jesus is “…the firstborn from the dead…” and that is a big deal, friends. Later in this same chapter He says, “I was dead, and behold, now I am alive forever and ever!” (Revelation 1:18). So the Lord's story goes through the grave and comes out the other side.

The answer is kingdom. John says Jesus “…has made us to be a kingdom, priests to His God and Father…” That's a big description for ordinary people, friends, and the text hands it to them. Jesus is the One who made them that, not anything they cooked up themselves.

The answer is True. John says, “Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him…” That's not a private showing, friends, and nobody gets left out of the line of sight. Every eye means every eye.

The answer is those who pierced Him. After “…every eye will see Him…” John adds “…even those who pierced Him.” The text names them on purpose, so they're not left out of the seeing. Then it says “…all the tribes of the earth will mourn because of Him.”

The answer is True. John writes, “I am the Alpha and the Omega…” says the Lord God, who is and was and is to come, the Almighty. Notice that it's the Lord God speaking in His own voice, friends, not John. Verse 8 is a different speaker from the verses around it.
The answer is Patmos. John says he “…was on the island of Patmos…” Not a name you forget once you've read it, friends. Patmos is the place where he hears the voice behind him.
The answer is True. John says he was on Patmos “…because of the word of God and my testimony about Jesus.” He doesn't give any other reason, friends. I won't add one, either.

The answer is False. The loud voice says, “Write on a scroll what you see and send it to the seven churches…” John is told to send it out, not keep it quiet. Write it on a scroll and send it, friends.

The answer is One like the Son of Man. John says, “…among the lampstands was One like the Son of Man…” In the Gospels, Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). So this is a lot to take in, friends, and John says it with care.
The answer is the sun. John says, “His face was like the sun shining at its brightest.” That's the picture John gives us of His face, friends. The sun at its brightest, and nothing else.

The answer is that John falls at His feet like a dead man. John says, “When I saw Him, I fell at His feet like a dead man.” That's his honest reaction, friends, and I think anyone would struggle to stay standing. Then comes the next part, where a hand is placed on him.
The answer is “Do not be afraid.” He puts His right hand on John and says those words first. Those are the words that come with His hand, friends. Comfort comes before the rest of what He says.

The answer is Death. He says, “…I hold the keys of Death and of Hades.” Right before that, He says, “I was dead, and behold, now I am alive forever and ever!” So the One who was dead holds its keys, friends.

The answer is the things that are and that will happen after this. He says, “Therefore write down the things you have seen, the things that are, and the things that will happen after this.” That's three sets of things to write, friends: what John has seen, what is, and what will happen after. So he has plenty of scroll work ahead.

The answer is True. He says, “…the seven lampstands are the seven churches.” It was a mystery, friends, and then He explains it right away. And remember where He was standing in the vision: among those lampstands.

The answer is the angels of the seven churches. He says, “The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches…” The stars are the ones He held in His right hand, friends. That's the detail from verse 16, explained in verse 20.
